chunks: And by this chain, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Abu Aqil Isa ibn Nasr, who said: Ali ibn Ziyad al-Sa'imuri wrote requesting a burial shroud, so he was written to: 'You will need it in the year eighty.' He died in the year eighty, and a shroud was sent to him before his death.

key_terms.الصَّائِمُرِيُّ: Al-Sa'imuri, a nisba indicating origin or tribe
key_terms.سَنَةٍ ثَمَانِينَ: The year eighty (of the Hijri calendar)
key_terms.عَلِيُّ بْنُ زِيَادٍ: Ali ibn Ziyad, the subject of the story

ai.seo_question: What is the story of Ali ibn Ziyad al-Sa'imuri and the burial shroud in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narrative from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* illustrates the Imam’s knowledge of the unseen (*‘ilm al-ghayb*) during the Minor Occultation, specifically regarding Ali ibn Ziyad al-Sa'imuri. The Imam’s precise prediction that the shroud would be needed in the year 80 AH, followed by its timely dispatch before death, serves as a key miracle (*karama*) validating the Imam’s spiritual authority and foresight. This event underscores the continuity of divine guidance and care for the faithful even during the period of concealment.
